claim: SLC26A9 contributes to airway surface hydration and gastric acid production.
source: The epithelial anion transporter SLC26A9 contributes to airway surface hydration and gastric acid production.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about SLC26A9 function.

claim: SLC26A9 colocalizes with CFTR.
source: Colocalizing with CFTR, SLC26A9 has been proposed as a target for the treatment of cystic fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: SLC26A9 has been proposed as a target for the treatment of cystic fibrosis.
source: Colocalizing with CFTR, SLC26A9 has been proposed as a target for the treatment of cystic fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Balázs and Mall, 2018; Mall and Galietta, 2015).

claim: The cryo-EM structures define the general architecture of eukaryotic SLC26 family members.
source: These structures define the general architecture of eukaryotic SLC26 family members and reveal an unusual mode of oligomerization which relies predominantly on the cytosolic STAS domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Slc26a9 exhibits an unusual mode of oligomerization which relies predominantly on the cytosolic STAS domain.
source: These structures define the general architecture of eukaryotic SLC26 family members and reveal an unusual mode of oligomerization which relies predominantly on the cytosolic STAS domain.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis showing that 89% of the dimer interface involves STAS domains.

claim: Slc26a9 mediates uncoupled chloride transport with negligible bicarbonate or sulfate permeability.
source: Our data illustrates conformational transitions of Slc26a9, supporting a rapid alternate-access mechanism which mediates uncoupled chloride transport with negligible bicarbonate or sulfate permeability.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data showing reversal potentials close to the Nernst potential of Cl- and negligible permeabilities for HCO3- and SO42-.

claim: Slc26a9 operates via a rapid alternate-access mechanism.
source: Our data illustrates conformational transitions of Slc26a9, supporting a rapid alternate-access mechanism which mediates uncoupled chloride transport with negligible bicarbonate or sulfate permeability.
evidence: This is supported by structural data showing inward-facing and intermediate conformations, and functional data showing saturation kinetics.

claim: A selective anion binding site is located in the center of a mobile module within the transmembrane domain.
source: The characterization of structure-guided mutants illuminates the properties of the ion transport path, including a selective anion binding site located in the center of a mobile module within the transmembrane domain.
evidence: This is supported by structural analysis and mutagenesis studies showing the location and properties of the binding site.

claim: SLC26A9 is found abundantly in the epithelia of lung and stomach.
source: It is found abundantly in the epithelia of lung and stomach (Chang et al., 2009b; Lohi et al., 2002; Xu et al., 2005), where it mediates luminal electrogenic chloride transport and contributes to airway clearance and the production of gastric acid.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: SLC26A9 mediates luminal electrogenic chloride transport.
source: It is found abundantly in the epithelia of lung and stomach (Chang et al., 2009b; Lohi et al., 2002; Xu et al., 2005), where it mediates luminal electrogenic chloride transport and contributes to airway clearance and the production of gastric acid.
evidence: This is supported by citations and functional data in the manuscript.

claim: Slc26a9-/- knockout mice develop airway and gastrointestinal pathologies.
source: Slc26a9–/– knockout mice develop airway and gastrointestinal pathologies (Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2008), and human genetic polymorphisms in SLC26A9 are correlated with altered severity of airway clearance disorders (Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012; Miller et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Human genetic polymorphisms in SLC26A9 are correlated with altered severity of airway clearance disorders.
source: Slc26a9–/– knockout mice develop airway and gastrointestinal pathologies (Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2008), and human genetic polymorphisms in SLC26A9 are correlated with altered severity of airway clearance disorders (Anagnostopoulou et al., 2012; Miller et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: SLC26A9 co-localizes with CFTR.
source: Owing to these associations, as well as its co-localization and proposed regulatory interactions with the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) (Avella et al., 2011; Bertrand et al., 2017; Bertrand et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009a; Strug et al., 2016), SLC26A9 has been proposed as a therapeutic target for treating complications associated with cystic fibrosis and other diseases of the airways and gastrointestinal tract (Balázs and Mall, 2018; Mall and Galietta, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: SLC26A9 has proposed regulatory interactions with CFTR.
source: Owing to these associations, as well as its co-localization and proposed regulatory interactions with the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) (Avella et al., 2011; Bertrand et al., 2017; Bertrand et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009a; Strug et al., 2016), SLC26A9 has been proposed as a therapeutic target for treating complications associated with cystic fibrosis and other diseases of the airways and gastrointestinal tract (Balázs and Mall, 2018; Mall and Galietta, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The ten functional SLC26 paralogs expressed in mammals are targeted to specific tissues and show a distinct transport mechanism and substrate preference.
source: The ten functional SLC26 paralogs expressed in mammals are targeted to specific tissues and show a distinct transport mechanism and substrate preference (Alper and Sharma, 2013), with the human ortholog SLC26A5 (Prestin) having insignificant transport function and instead operating as voltage-dependent motor protein which is responsible for electromotility in cochlear outer hair cells (Dallos and Fakler, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: SLC26A5 (Prestin) has insignificant transport function and instead operates as a voltage-dependent motor protein responsible for electromotility in cochlear outer hair cells.
source: The ten functional SLC26 paralogs expressed in mammals are targeted to specific tissues and show a distinct transport mechanism and substrate preference (Alper and Sharma, 2013), with the human ortholog SLC26A5 (Prestin) having insignificant transport function and instead operating as voltage-dependent motor protein which is responsible for electromotility in cochlear outer hair cells (Dallos and Fakler, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Some reports provide evidence of chloride/bicarbonate exchange by SLC26A9.
source: The transport mode of SLC26A9 is controversial, with some reports providing evidence of chloride/bicarbonate exchange (Chang et al., 2009b; Xu et al., 2005), yet others claiming that SLC26A9 has negligible bicarbonate permeability and instead confers an uncoupled, constitutively-active, channel-like Cl– conductance (Bertrand et al., 2009; Dorwart et al., 2007; Loriol et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Some reports claim that SLC26A9 has negligible bicarbonate permeability and instead confers an uncoupled, constitutively-active, channel-like Cl- conductance.
source: The transport mode of SLC26A9 is controversial, with some reports providing evidence of chloride/bicarbonate exchange (Chang et al., 2009b; Xu et al., 2005), yet others claiming that SLC26A9 has negligible bicarbonate permeability and instead confers an uncoupled, constitutively-active, channel-like Cl– conductance (Bertrand et al., 2009; Dorwart et al., 2007; Loriol et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Uncoupled Cl- transport has been reported for SLC26A7.
source: Although less characterized, uncoupled Cl– transport has also been reported for SLC26A7 (Kim et al., 2005) and SLC26A11 (Rahmati et al., 2013) whereas evidence for mixed uncoupled and coupled exchange properties was shown for SLC26A3 and SLC26A6 (Ohana et al., 2011; Shcheynikov et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Uncoupled Cl- transport has been reported for SLC26A11.
source: Although less characterized, uncoupled Cl– transport has also been reported for SLC26A7 (Kim et al., 2005) and SLC26A11 (Rahmati et al., 2013) whereas evidence for mixed uncoupled and coupled exchange properties was shown for SLC26A3 and SLC26A6 (Ohana et al., 2011; Shcheynikov et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Evidence for mixed uncoupled and coupled exchange properties was shown for SLC26A3 and SLC26A6.
source: Although less characterized, uncoupled Cl– transport has also been reported for SLC26A7 (Kim et al., 2005) and SLC26A11 (Rahmati et al., 2013) whereas evidence for mixed uncoupled and coupled exchange properties was shown for SLC26A3 and SLC26A6 (Ohana et al., 2011; Shcheynikov et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: No high-resolution structures have been reported for SLC26A9 or any other eukaryotic SLC26 family member prior to this study.
source: No high-resolution structures have yet been reported for SLC26A9 or any other eukaryotic SLC26 family member, and detailed structural information about a full-length SLC26 protein is limited to a single crystal structure of a bacterial fumarate transporter (SLC26Dg) (Geertsma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work, supported by citation.

claim: Detailed structural information about a full-length SLC26 protein is limited to a single crystal structure of a bacterial fumarate transporter (SLC26Dg).
source: No high-resolution structures have yet been reported for SLC26A9 or any other eukaryotic SLC26 family member, and detailed structural information about a full-length SLC26 protein is limited to a single crystal structure of a bacterial fumarate transporter (SLC26Dg) (Geertsma et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The monomeric SLC26Dg structure provided information about the basic elements of the SLC26 architecture consisting of a transport domain of 14 membrane-inserted α-helices and a C-terminal cytosolic STAS domain.
source: The monomeric SLC26Dg structure provided valuable information about the basic elements of the SLC26 architecture consisting of a transport domain of 14 membrane-inserted α-helices, and a C-terminal cytosolic STAS domain of unknown function.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the SLC26Dg structure.

claim: SLC26 transporters assemble into functional oligomers.
source: However, SLC26 transporters assemble into functional oligomers (Compton et al., 2014; Detro-Dassen et al., 2008; Zheng et al., 2006), and the quaternary arrangement of an oligomeric eukaryotic SLC26 transporter has remained unknown.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The quaternary arrangement of an oligomeric eukaryotic SLC26 transporter was unknown prior to this study.
source: However, SLC26 transporters assemble into functional oligomers (Compton et al., 2014; Detro-Dassen et al., 2008; Zheng et al., 2006), and the quaternary arrangement of an oligomeric eukaryotic SLC26 transporter has remained unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this work.

claim: Slc26a9T exhibits greater surface expression compared to full-length Slc26a9.
source: A striking observation from HEK293 cells expressing fluorescently-tagged Slc26a9T is that the truncations have apparently resulted in greater surface expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy images showing greater membrane-attributable fluorescence for Slc26a9T.

claim: The IVS might be responsible for the retention of full-length Slc26a9 in intracellular membranes.
source: This is also observed for a construct only lacking the IVS (SLC26A9ΔIVS), but not for a construct solely lacking the CT (SLC26A9ΔCT), thus suggesting that the IVS might be responsible for the retention of the protein in intracellular membranes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the surface expression of different truncation constructs.

claim: Slc26a9T can be purified to homogeneity in a dimeric state.
source: Relative to the full-length protein, Slc26a9T exhibits several additional favorable qualities, including more efficient detergent extraction and the capacity to be purified to homogeneity in a dimeric state (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography and SDS-PAGE data.

claim: Purified Slc26a9T reconstituted into lipid vesicles exhibits robust Cl- transport activity.
source: To assess whether Slc26a9T retains transport activity, the purified protein was reconstituted into lipid vesicles and tested for electrogenic Cl– transport using a fluorometric assay (Kane Dickson et al., 2014). In these experiments, we observed robust transport activity that can be diminished in a dose-dependent manner by a known inhibitor of Slc26a9, implying that neither the removal of the IDRs from the STAS domain nor the purification procedure has compromised the function of Slc26a9T (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorometric assay data showing Cl- transport.

claim: Slc26a9T transport activity can be diminished in a dose-dependent manner by a known inhibitor.
source: In these experiments, we observed robust transport activity that can be diminished in a dose-dependent manner by a known inhibitor of Slc26a9, implying that neither the removal of the IDRs from the STAS domain nor the purification procedure has compromised the function of Slc26a9T (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response data for DIDS inhibition.

claim: Slc26a9T does not require the presence of endogenous cellular factors for its activity.
source: Observation of Cl– transport by reconstituted Slc26a9T also demonstrates that the protein does not require the presence of endogenous cellular factors for its activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of transport activity in reconstituted proteoliposomes.

claim: Slc26a9T exhibits constitutively active, anion-selective currents with linear current-voltage relationships in whole-cell recordings.
source: In the whole-cell configuration, both constructs yield constitutively active, anion-selective currents with linear current-voltage (I-V) relationships, as reported previously for human SLC26A9 (Bertrand et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009b; Dorwart et al., 2007; Loriol et al., 2008) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data.

claim: Slc26a9T-transfected cells show raw currents which are, on average, at least four-fold larger than currents associated with full-length Slc26a9.
source: As expected from the higher surface expression, Slc26a9T-transfected cells show raw currents which are, on average, at least four-fold larger than currents associated with full-length Slc26a9 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is supported by whole-cell patch-clamp data comparing the two constructs.

claim: Slc26a9T currents in inside-out patches are constitutive and exhibit a linear I-V relationship.
source: Moreover, whereas we could not reliably measure macroscopic currents in inside-out patches from full-length Slc26a9-transfected cells, robust activity was observed for Slc26a9T (Figure 1B). As for whole-cell experiments, these currents are constitutive and exhibit a linear I-V relationship.
evidence: This is supported by inside-out patch-clamp data.

claim: No discrete single-channel transitions were observed in any of the recordings of Slc26a9T.
source: Contrary to a previous study (Chang et al., 2009b), we did not observe any discrete single-channel transitions in any of our recordings.
evidence: This is a negative result from electrophysiology experiments.

claim: Slc26a9T currents reverse very close to the Nernst potential of Cl- under different NaCl gradients.
source: To assess the relative anion/cation selectivity, we measured I-V relationships for inside-out patches of Slc26a9T-expressing cells that were subjected to different NaCl gradients. In all cases, the currents reverse very close to the Nernst potential of Cl–, implying that Cl– is the only transported charge in the system and excluding obligate coupling to other ions (Figure 1C; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is supported by reversal potential measurements under various ionic gradients.

claim: Cl- is the only transported charge in the Slc26a9T system, excluding obligate coupling to other ions.
source: In all cases, the currents reverse very close to the Nernst potential of Cl–, implying that Cl– is the only transported charge in the system and excluding obligate coupling to other ions (Figure 1C; Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is inferred from reversal potential data.

claim: Slc26a9T shows saturation of currents at high Cl- concentrations with a Km of 30 mM.
source: Next, we evaluated the relationship between substrate concentration and ion flux and found a saturation of currents at high Cl– concentrations (with a Km of 30 mM, Figure 1D), consistent with a weak interaction of the protein with its transported ion.
evidence: This is supported by conductance-concentration relationship data.

claim: The Km of Cl- for Slc26a9T (30 mM) is similar to that described for the Cl-/HCO3- exchanger SLC4A1/Band 3 (~46 mM).
source: Although the high Cl– selectivity, fast kinetics, and weak substrate interaction would all be consistent with a channel-like mechanism, they do not exclude transport by an alternate-exchange mechanism, since a similar high Km for Cl– (i.e. ~46 mM) was described for the rapid Cl–/HCO3– exchanger SLC4A1/Band 3 (Liu et al., 1996).
evidence: This is a comparison to a known transporter, supported by citation.

claim: The permeability sequence of Slc26a9T is SCN->I->Br->NO3->Cl-, following a lyotropic series.
source: The observed permeability sequence (SCN–>I–>Br– > NO3–>Cl–) follows a lyotropic series (Wright and Diamond, 1977), which favors more easily dehydrated anions (Figure 1E; Figure 1—figure supplement 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by bi-ionic substitution experiments.

claim: Slc26a9T has negligible permeabilities for F-, HCO3-, and SO42-.
source: In contrast, we measured negligible permeabilities for the anions F–, HCO3–, and SO42– (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by bi-ionic substitution experiments showing no significant permeability.

claim: The permeability sequence of Slc26a9T agrees with previous measurements of human SLC26A9 from oocyte voltage-clamp experiments.
source: The permeability sequence agrees with previous measurements of human SLC26A9 derived from oocyte voltage-clamp experiments (Dorwart et al., 2007; Loriol et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: The absence of HCO3- permeability in Slc26a9T contrasts with some reports showing evidence of Cl-/HCO3- exchange.
source: However, the absence of HCO3– permeability is in contrast to some reports showing evidence of Cl–/HCO3– exchange by Slc26a9 which were based on measurements of intracellular pH changes in response to removal of external Cl– in the presence of bath HCO3– (Chang et al., 2009b; Xu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: All reports of electrogenic transport by Slc26a9 indicate negligible movement of HCO3-.
source: While we cannot fully account for this discrepancy we note that all reports of electrogenic transport indicate negligible movement of HCO3–.
evidence: This is a statement about the consensus in the literature.

claim: The conductivity sequence of Slc26a9T is Cl->Br->NO3-~SCN->I-.
source: To assess relative transport rates, macroscopic conductance ratios (Gx/GCl) of permeable anions revealed a conductivity sequence of Cl–>Br– > NO3–~SCN–>I– (Figure 1F; Figure 1—figure supplement 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by conductance ratio measurements from bi-ionic substitution experiments.

claim: The conductivity pattern of Slc26a9T deviates from the permeability sequence, with Cl- being considerably more conductive than any other tested anion.
source: Notably, the conductivity pattern deviates from the permeability sequence, with Cl– being considerably more conductive than any other tested anion.
evidence: This is observed from comparing permeability and conductance data.

claim: The high relative permeability of lyotropic anions shows that they face a lower energy barrier for dehydration and entry into the transport pathway compared with Cl-.
source: The high relative permeability of lyotropic anions shows that they face a lower energy barrier for dehydration and entry into the transport pathway compared with Cl–, while their lower relative conductance implies that they also encounter a deeper energy well, which in turn would decrease their overall turnover rate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the permeability and conductance data.

claim: Lyotropic anions encounter a deeper energy well in Slc26a9T, which decreases their overall turnover rate.
source: The high relative permeability of lyotropic anions shows that they face a lower energy barrier for dehydration and entry into the transport pathway compared with Cl–, while their lower relative conductance implies that they also encounter a deeper energy well, which in turn would decrease their overall turnover rate.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the permeability and conductance data.

claim: SCN- has a lower Km and Vmax compared to Cl- in Slc26a9T.
source: These properties are also reflected in the lower Km and Vmax of SCN– compared to Cl– (Figure 1D) and suggest that Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl– transporter.
evidence: This is supported by conductance-concentration relationship data.

claim: Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl- transporter.
source: These properties are also reflected in the lower Km and Vmax of SCN– compared to Cl– (Figure 1D) and suggest that Slc26a9 has evolved as an efficient uncoupled Cl– transporter.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional properties observed.

claim: The structure of Slc26a9T was determined by cryo-EM at 3.96 Å resolution in detergent.
source: A 3.96 Å dataset of Slc26a9T purified in the synthetic digitonin analogue glyco-diosgenin (GDN) was of high quality and allowed the unambiguous interpretation of the cryo-EM density by an atomic model (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2; Table 1; Video 1).
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data and model refinement statistics.

claim: The structure of Slc26a9T was determined in lipid nanodiscs at 7.77 Å resolution.
source: To exclude a possible bias from a detergent environment, we have in parallel reconstituted the purified protein into lipid nanodiscs and determined its structure at low (7.77 Å) resolution (Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 4; Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by cryo-EM data from nanodisc-reconstituted protein.

claim: Both detergent and nanodisc datasets display similar general features of the protein with respect to the organization of subunits and their oligomeric arrangement.
source: Both datasets display similar general features of the protein with respect to the organization of subunits and their oligomeric arrangement, although the nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
evidence: This is observed from comparing the two cryo-EM structures.

claim: The nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
source: Both datasets display similar general features of the protein with respect to the organization of subunits and their oligomeric arrangement, although the nanodisc structure reveals localized rigid-body movements indicative of a different functional conformation.
evidence: This is observed from comparing the two cryo-EM structures.

claim: Slc26a9T is a dimer of elongated shape that is approximately 100 Å long and 50 Å wide.
source: The protein is a dimer of elongated shape that is approximately 100 Å long and 50 Å wide (Video 3).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The STAS domains of Slc26a9T protrude 38 Å into the cytosol.
source: The interacting domain-swapped STAS domains, appearing as a knob centered on one side of Slc26a9T particles, protrude 38 Å into the cytosol, while a spiky loop on each subunit projects towards the extracellular solution (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplements 1–4).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The interactions between both subunits of the dimeric Slc26a9T are highly unusual since they only exhibit minimal contacts between the membrane-inserted domains.
source: The interactions between both subunits of the dimeric protein are highly unusual since, unlike other proteins with a similar fold, they only exhibit minimal contacts between the membrane–inserted domains at the intracellular end of the last transmembrane helix (Figure 2).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and comparison to other proteins.

claim: Only 11% of the buried surface in the Slc26a9T dimer can be attributed to interactions directly between the transmembrane domains.
source: Of the 8'114 Å2 of the combined molecular surface buried in the dimer, only 11% can be attributed to interactions directly between the transmembrane domains (TMDs).
evidence: This is calculated from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: 16% of the buried surface in the Slc26a9T dimer is contributed by mutual contacts between STAS domains.
source: Conversely, 16% of the buried surface is contributed by mutual contacts between STAS domains whereas the remaining interactions are mutually formed between the swapped STAS domain and the transmembrane part of the opposing subunit.
evidence: This is calculated from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The extended N-terminus of Slc26a9T binds to the STAS domain and appears to contribute to dimer stability.
source: Another remarkable feature of the dimer interface concerns the binding of the extended N-terminus to the STAS domain, which appears to contribute to dimer stability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: In the Slc26a9T dimer, the cytoplasmic STAS domains act as a platform for interactions between subunits.
source: In the Slc26a9T dimer, the cytoplasmic STAS domains act as a platform for interactions between subunits, thus explaining the deleterious transport phenotype observed upon mutations or its removal in different family members (Babu et al., 2010; Dorwart et al., 2008a; Geertsma et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2011) (Figure 3, Video 3).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claim: The STAS domain of Slc26a9T closely resembles known STAS domain structures from eukaryotic SLC26A5 (Prestin) and the bacterial homolog SLC26Dg.
source: This cytoplasmic unit closely resembles known STAS domain structures from eukaryotic SLC26A5 (Prestin) (Lolli et al., 2016; Pasqualetto et al., 2010) and the bacterial homolog SLC26Dg (Geertsma et al., 2015) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claim: The STAS domain consists of a six-stranded mixed β-sheet core decorated with four interspersed α-helices.
source: It consists of a six-stranded mixed β-sheet core, which is decorated with four interspersed α-helices (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Several loop regions of the STAS domain make contacts with the TMD of the opposing subunit at parts close to the membrane.
source: Several of the loop regions connecting β-strands with their adjoining α-helices (i.e. the β3-Cα1, β4-Cα2, β5-Cα3 and the Cα3-β6 loops) make contacts between the STAS domains and the TMD of the opposing subunit at parts that are close to the membrane (at the α4-α5, α8-α9, α12- α13 loops and the terminal helix α14) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The strong conservation of residues at the contact region between STAS and TMD points towards the preservation of this interface among family members.
source: The strong conservation of residues at the contact region with the TMD points towards the preservation of this interface among family members (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is inferred from sequence alignment and structural analysis.

claim: At the bottom part of the STAS dimer, interactions with the N-terminus are mediated by the β1-β2, β2-β3 and β6-Cα4 loops.
source: At the bottom part of the STAS dimer, interactions with the N-terminus are mediated by the β1-β2, β2-β3 and β6-Cα4 loops (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: A negatively charged groove at the dimer interface of the STAS domain could potentially interact with cellular factors.
source: Between both regions, on the side of the STAS dimer, a negatively charged groove at the dimer interface could potentially interact with cellular factors (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E,F).
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis showing a charged surface.

claim: In the dimeric architecture of the STAS domain, the two unstructured regions removed in Slc26a9T would be located opposite to the dimer-interface and thus be available for interactions with accessory proteins.
source: Finally, in the observed dimeric architecture of the STAS domain, the two unstructured regions removed in the Slc26a9T construct would be located opposite to the dimer-interface and thus be available for interactions with accessory proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is inferred from the structure of the truncated construct.

claim: The overall architecture of the TMD conforms to the 7+7 inverted repeat topology.
source: The overall architecture of the TMD conforms to the 7 + 7 inverted repeat topology (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which was previously observed in the structure of the prokaryotic homologue SLC26Dg (Geertsma et al., 2015) and in members of the distantly related SLC4 (Arakawa et al., 2015; Huynh et al., 2018) and SLC23 (Alguel et al., 2016; Lu et al., 2011) families.
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and comparison to other structures.

claim: The Slc26a9T TMD is composed of 14 membrane-inserted α-helices, with α8-14 representing a similar yet inverted organization to α1-7.
source: Consistent with the known features of this arrangement, the Slc26a9T TMD is composed of 14 membrane-inserted α-helices, with α8–14 representing a similar yet inverted organization to α1–7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The TMD is segregated into two subdomains: a convex core module (consisting of α1-4 and 9-11) carrying a putative ion-binding site, and a concave gate module (consisting of α5-7 and 12-14).
source: The TMD is segregated into two subdomains, a convex core module (consisting of α1–4, and 9–11) carrying a putative ion-binding site, and a concave gate module (consisting of α5–7 and 12–14) (Figure 4, Video 3).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Both core and gate modules constitute independent structural units that interact via an extended interface.
source: Both modules constitute independent structural units that interact via an extended interface (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The TMD of Slc26a9T shows a high degree of similarity to its equivalent unit of SLC26Dg (RMSD of 2.0 Å).
source: Although displaying channel-like functional properties, the structure of the TMD of Slc26a9T shows hallmarks of a transporter. The striking degree of similarity revealed from a superposition with its equivalent unit of SLC26Dg (RMSD of 2.0 Å) emphasizes the high conservation within the family and suggests that both structures display equivalent conformations (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is observed from structural superposition.

claim: The large cavity between gate and core modules is accessible from the intracellular side but does not extend into a contiguous pore region towards the extracellular side.
source: The large cavity between gate and core modules is accessible from the intracellular side but does not extend into a contiguous pore region towards the extracellular side, suggesting that the Slc26a9T structure represents an inward-open state of the protein that facilitates transport by an alternate-access mechanism.
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The Slc26a9T structure in detergent represents an inward-open state of the protein.
source: The large cavity between gate and core modules is accessible from the intracellular side but does not extend into a contiguous pore region towards the extracellular side, suggesting that the Slc26a9T structure represents an inward-open state of the protein that facilitates transport by an alternate-access mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from structural features.

claim: The nanodisc TMD structure differs from the detergent structure in the conformation of the core module, which has rotated by approximately 14° and moved by 4 Å towards the extracellular side.
source: This assumption is further supported by the comparison of TMDs of Slc26a9T from cryo-EM maps acquired either in detergent micelles or lipid nanodiscs (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C–E). The nanodisc TMD structure differs in the conformation of the core module, which has rotated as rigid body by approximately 14° and moved by 4 Å towards the extracellular side, whereas the remainder of the protein appears largely unaltered.
evidence: This is observed from comparing the two cryo-EM structures.

claim: The nanodisc structure likely shows an intermediate state of the protein on its transition towards an outward-facing state.
source: This conformation thus likely shows an intermediate state of the protein on its transition towards an outward-facing state (Figure 5D; Video 4).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the detergent and nanodisc structures.

claim: A loop-helix structure connecting α5-α6 (α5') fills a depression in the structure created by the short α13-α14 turn.
source: First, a loop-helix structure connecting α5-α6 (α5') fills a depression in the structure created by the short α13–α14 turn, which would not otherwise reach the boundary of the outer leaflet of an undistorted bilayer (Figures 4B and 5B).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The loop region connecting α3 and the extended α4 protrudes into the extracellular space and contains two predicted glycosylation sites near the tip.
source: A second distinguishing feature of Slc26a9T concerns the loop region connecting α3 and the extended α4, which protrudes into the extracellular space and which contains two predicted glycosylation sites (Li et al., 2014) near the tip of the spiky extension (Figures 4C and 5C).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure and supported by a citation about glycosylation sites.

claim: The extended N-terminus of Slc26a9T is significantly longer than the equivalent region in SLC26Dg.
source: Finally, the extended N-terminus of Slc26a9T, preceding α1, is significantly longer than the equivalent region in SLC26Dg (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claim: The N-terminus of Slc26a9T is partly mobile and contains extended regions with interspersed secondary structure elements.
source: In the mammalian transporter, the N-terminus is partly mobile and contains extended regions with interspersed secondary structure elements.
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: A structured part of the N-terminus preceding α1 forms scattered helical segments peripherally contacting the inner membrane leaflet and containing several basic residues.
source: Whereas the initial part of the N-terminus engages in the earlier described interaction with the STAS domains, a mobile linker bridges this region to a structured part preceding α1, which forms scattered helical segments peripherally contacting the inner membrane leaflet and containing several basic residues (Figure 5C, bottom inset).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Due to high sequence conservation between paralogs, the three structural features (α5', extracellular loop, extended N-terminus) are likely preserved in mammalian SLC26 transporters.
source: Due to the high sequence conservation between paralogs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), all three structural features are likely preserved in mammalian SLC26 transporters.
evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation.

claim: In the inward-facing conformation, transported anions enter the protein via a wide aqueous vestibule, attracted by positive electrostatic potential from basic amino acids at its intracellular entrance.
source: In the observed inward-facing conformation of the TMD, transported anions enter the protein to access their binding site via a wide aqueous vestibule, presumably attracted by the positive electrostatic potential that is conferred by an excess of basic amino acids at its intracellular entrance (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is observed from the structure and supported by electrostatic calculations.

claim: For wild-type Slc26a9T, the linear I-V relationship is compatible with symmetric rate-limiting barriers on the transport cycle in the absence of applied voltage.
source: For wild-type (WT) Slc26a9T, the linear I-V relationship is compatible with symmetric rate-limiting barriers on the transport cycle in the absence of applied voltage (Lam and Dutzler, 2018; Paulino et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the I-V relationship and supported by citations.

claim: Mutations R205E or K358E minimally perturb the linear I-V relationship of Slc26a9T.
source: This linear relation is minimally perturbed upon introducing the mutations R205E or K358E, which are positioned at the outermost regions of the intracellular vestibule (Figure 6A; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claim: Mutations K270E and K443E, located deeper in the intracellular cavity, display considerable outward rectification.
source: In contrast, mutations K270E and K443E, located deeper in the intracellular cavity and close to the presumed anion binding site, both altered the electrostatics and displayed considerable outward rectification (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claim: The outward rectification in K270E and K443E mutants indicates a relative increase of the inward barrier.
source: This behavior indicates a relative increase of the inward barrier by either impeding the access of anions from the intracellular side or alternatively by hampering conformational transitions of the protein.
evidence: This is inferred from the electrophysiology data.

claim: Mutation of extracellular basic residues K221 and K431 leads to inward rectification.
source: Complimentary to the intracellular charge-reversal mutations, we find a reciprocal effect leading to inward rectification upon mutation of extracellular basic residues K221 and K431 that are predicted to line the aqueous cavity to the binding site in an outward-facing conformation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claim: An anion binding site is inferred to be located in a pocket of the core domain between the N-termini of the membrane-inserted partial helices α3 and α10.
source: Although in our cryo-EM reconstructions we did not observe any density attributable to bound Cl–, its absence is concordant with its measured low apparent affinity. We infer an anion binding site to be located in a pocket of the core domain between the N-termini of the membrane-inserted partial helices α3 and α10 (Figures 4C and 7A; Video 5).
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and comparison to related transporters.

claim: The equivalent location to the inferred Slc26a9 binding site was proposed as a substrate-binding site for the fumarate-proton symporter SLC26Dg and the chloride-bicarbonate transporter SLC4A1/Band 3.
source: The equivalent location was proposed as a substrate-binding site for the fumarate-proton symporter SLC26Dg (Chang et al., 2019a) and the chloride-bicarbonate transporter SLC4A1/Band 3 (Arakawa et al., 2015) and confirmed for the SLC23 transporters UraA (Lu et al., 2011) and UapA (Alguel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The binding site is ideally positioned at the apex of the inward-open cavity, with dual pseudo-symmetrically related helix dipoles arranged in a manner frequently observed for binding sites of anion transporters.
source: This site would be ideally positioned at the apex of the inward-open cavity, with its dual pseudo-symmetrically related helix dipoles arranged in a manner frequently observed for binding sites of anion transporters (Dutzler et al., 2002; Screpanti and Hunte, 2007) (Figures 4C and 7A).
evidence: This is observed from structural analysis and supported by citations.

claim: Compared to SLC26Dg, the pocket of Slc26a9T is considerably smaller due to the conformation of F128 projecting its side-chain into the pocket.
source: Compared to SLC26Dg, the pocket of Slc26a9T is considerably smaller, as a consequence of the conformation of F128 projecting its side-chain into the pocket, thus creating a site of appropriate size for a Cl– ion (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claim: Residues F128, F92, and L391 contribute to the partly hydrophobic character of the binding site, which likely accounts for the observed lyotropic permeability sequence of anions.
source: In this site, several residues could plausibly interact with the transported substrates. Besides F128, these include the nonpolar residues F92 and L391, all contributing to the partly hydrophobic character frequently found in anion binding sites which likely account for the observed lyotropic permeability sequence of anions (Figure 1E) (Dani et al., 1983; Dutzler et al., 2002).
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and supported by citations.

claim: Dehydrated anions could be stabilized by side-chain interactions with Q88, S392, and possibly T127, as well as main-chain interactions at the N-terminus of α10.
source: Dehydrated anions could be stabilized by side-chain interactions with Q88, S392, and possibly T127, as well as main-chain interactions at the N-terminus of α10, which together form a cradle to coordinate the desolvated ion (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis.

claim: Several binding-site mutants altered the linear I-V relationship, with S392A showing inward rectification and F128A and Q88A showing outward rectification.
source: To probe the functional importance of potential binding-site residues for anion interactions, we individually mutated them to alanine and used inside-out patch recordings to assess any corresponding changes in transport behavior (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–G). Several mutants altered the linear I-V relationship, with the resulting inward rectification of the mutant S392A indicating a relative increase of the outer barrier and conversely, the outward rectification in the mutants F128A and Q88A, a relative increase of the inner barrier during transport (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,D,F).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claim: Only minor perturbations of the linear I-V relationship are found for the binding site residues F92A and L391A.
source: In contrast, only minor perturbations of the linear I–V relationship are found for the binding site residues F92A and L391A and no change is observed for the mutant N441A residing on the gate module, which, although proximal to the site, is not predicted to participate in ion coordination (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,E,G).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on mutants.

claim: The mutant Q88E shows severely decreased currents that are strongly outward-rectifying, consistent with compromised transport activity due to interference of the negatively charged residue with transported anions.
source: The change in the conductance properties upon mutation of Gln 88 is even more pronounced in the mutant Q88E, which replaces the amino acid conserved in mammalian paralogs with a negatively charged residue found in several prokaryotic transporters (Geertsma et al., 2015). Despite the strong apparent surface expression and high stability of the mutant, there are no currents observed in excised patches and severely decreased currents in whole-cell measurements are strongly outward-rectifying, consistent with a compromised transport activity due to the interference of the negatively charged residue with the transported anions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H,I).
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data on the mutant.

claim: Changes in the inverted relationship between permeability and conductivity are most pronounced for S392A and F128A, where chloride becomes less conductive than other permeant anions.
source: Although affected in all binding-site mutants (Figure 7—figure supplements 2 and 3A–E; Table 2), changes are most pronounced for S392A and F128A, where chloride becomes less conductive than other permeant anions, a behavior that is also reflected in the kinetic parameters obtained from the concentration dependence of transport of Cl– and SCN– (Figure 7C–H; Figure 7—figure supplement 3; Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by bi-ionic substitution and conductance-concentration data on mutants.

claim: The mutant L391A shows a pronounced increase in the Km of SCN- by nearly two orders of magnitude.
source: A pronounced difference is also observed for the mutant L391A where the Km of SCN– increases by nearly two orders of magnitude (Figure 7—figure supplement 3I; Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by conductance-concentration data on the mutant.

claim: In no case did binding-site mutants show major increases in permeation by either HCO3- or SO42-, nor evidence of coupled transport.
source: Whereas the strong effect of different binding-site mutants on conduction underlines their importance for anion transport, in no case did we detect major increases in permeation by either HCO3– or SO42–, nor did we observe any evidence of coupled transport (Figure 7—figure supplements 1A–G and 2; Table 2).
evidence: This is supported by bi-ionic substitution data on mutants.

claim: The dimeric organization of Slc26a9 differs markedly from structurally related transport proteins of the SLC4 and SLC23 families, which interact via an extended interface between gate modules.
source: The dimeric organization of Slc26a9 differs markedly from structurally related transport proteins of the SLC4 and SLC23 families, which interact via an extended interface between gate modules (Alguel et al., 2016; Arakawa et al., 2015; Chang and Geertsma, 2017; Huynh et al., 2018; Yu et al., 2017) (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is observed from structural comparison and supported by citations.

claim: In Slc26a9, the interface between the TMDs is minimal whereas the bulk of subunit interactions are mediated by the cytoplasmic STAS domains involving contacts with the N-terminus and intracellular loop regions of the gate module.
source: In contrast, in Slc26a9 the interface between the TMDs is minimal whereas the bulk of subunit interactions are mediated by the cytoplasmic STAS domains involving contacts with the N-terminus and intracellular loop regions of the gate module (Figure 2).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: A similar minimal contact relationship between transmembrane domains was recently proposed to underlie dimerization of the prokaryotic transporter SLC26Dg in a membrane environment, based on EPR-derived distance constraints.
source: A similar relationship between transmembrane domains was recently proposed to underlie dimerization of the prokaryotic transporter SLC26Dg in a membrane environment, based on EPR-derived distance constraints (Chang et al., 2019b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Minimal contacts in the membrane-inserted domain have been recently observed for the mechanosensitive channel OSCA, where subunit interactions are mediated exclusively between residues of the cytoplasmic domains.
source: Although such minimal contacts in the membrane-inserted domain are unusual for oligomeric membrane proteins, they have been recently observed for the mechanosensitive channel OSCA (Jojoa-Cruz et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2018), where subunit interactions are mediated exclusively between residues of the cytoplasmic domains.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Slc26a9 shows large uncoupled macroscopic Cl- currents that saturate only at high mM concentration.
source: As previously shown based on whole-cell experiments (Bertrand et al., 2009; Chang et al., 2009b; Dorwart et al., 2007; Loriol et al., 2008) and confirmed here with excised patches, Slc26a9 shows large uncoupled macroscopic Cl– currents that saturate only at high mM concentration.
evidence: This is supported by electrophysiology data and citations.

claim: The properties of Slc26a9 would be entirely consistent with a fast bidirectional uniport mechanism.
source: For this reason, the protein has been generally referred to as ion channel. However, such properties would be entirely consistent with a fast bidirectional uniport mechanism as evidenced by other structural and functional data shown in our study.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional and structural data.

claim: The high Km of Cl- matches its intracellular concentration and would foster high turnover leading to the observed conduction phenotype.
source: The high Km of Cl– matches its intracellular concentration and would foster high turnover leading to the observed conduction phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured Km and physiological Cl- concentrations.

claim: Transport of the hydrophobic ion SCN- saturates at lower concentration consistent with a mechanism mediated by an anion binding site.
source: Moreover, transport of the hydrophobic ion SCN– saturates at lower concentration consistent with a mechanism that is mediated by an anion binding site, which would be expected in a transporter.
evidence: This is inferred from the measured Km for SCN-.

claim: Structural data clearly suggest that Slc26a9 works by an alternate-access mechanism akin to other family members.
source: Additionally, our structural data clearly suggest that Slc26a9 works by an alternate-access mechanism akin to other family members.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing different conformations.

claim: The inward-facing structure of Slc26a9T shows the ion binding site accessible to the cytoplasm.
source: This is evidenced by a comparison between the inward-facing structure of Slc26a9T determined in detergent, where the ion binding site is accessible to the cytoplasm, and an intermediate conformation of the lipid nanodisc-reconstituted transporter, where an upward movement of the core module has caused the binding site to be buried between core and gate modules (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: In the intermediate conformation, an upward movement of the core module has caused the binding site to be buried between core and gate modules.
source: This is evidenced by a comparison between the inward-facing structure of Slc26a9T determined in detergent, where the ion binding site is accessible to the cytoplasm, and an intermediate conformation of the lipid nanodisc-reconstituted transporter, where an upward movement of the core module has caused the binding site to be buried between core and gate modules (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is observed from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: Both structures provide insight into conformational changes in which the relatively unconstrained core module makes ascending and descending rigid-body movements relative to the immobilized gate module-STAS domain complex, in a process that resembles the elevator transport mechanism.
source: In combination, both structures provide insight into conformational changes in which the relatively unconstrained core module, providing the substrate binding site, makes ascending and descending rigid-body movements relative to the immobilized gate module-STAS domain complex, in a process that resembles the elevator transport mechanism (Drew and Boudker, 2016; Ficici et al., 2017; Reyes et al., 2009) (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the two structures and supported by citations.

claim: Such an elevator-like mechanism would allow for fast transport kinetics as observed for Slc26a9T and as previously described for the Cl-/HCO3- transporter SLC4A1/Band 3.
source: Such mechanism would allow for fast transport kinetics as observed here and as previously described for the Cl–/HCO3– transporter SLC4A1/Band 3, which shares a similar architecture (Arakawa et al., 2015; Brahm, 1977).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural mechanism and supported by citations.

claim: The plausible homology to the known outward-facing structure of SLC4A1/Band 3 permits the anticipation of the possible extent of conformational changes in Slc26a9.
source: The plausible homology to the known outward-facing structure of SLC4A1/Band 3 (Arakawa et al., 2015) also permits the anticipation of the possible extent of conformational changes, where basic residues on the rim of the resulting extracellular vestibule likely create a positive electrostatic environment which is similar to that observed in the vestibule of the inward-facing state.
evidence: This is inferred from structural homology and supported by a citation.

claim: The role of electrostatics in the transport mechanism is supported by functional experiments and model-based calculations.
source: The role of electrostatics in this hypothesis is supported by functional experiments and model-based calculations (Figure 6A–C; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis data and Poisson-Boltzmann calculations.

claim: During transport, the negatively charged Cl- is dragged across the transmembrane electric field, thus likely facilitating conformational changes.
source: During transport, the negatively charged Cl– is dragged across the transmembrane electric field, thus likely facilitating conformational changes.
evidence: This is inferred from the electrostatic properties and transport mechanism.

claim: A similar mechanism may underlie the substrate-conferred electromotility observed in the homologous motor protein Prestin.
source: A similar mechanism may underlie the substrate-conferred electromotility observed in the homologous motor protein Prestin (Oliver et al., 2001).
evidence: This is speculated based on the mechanism observed for Slc26a9 and supported by a citation.

claim: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport SO42- is probably related to the fact that interactions within the binding site may not be sufficiently strong for the coordination of divalent anions.
source: The lyotropic permeability sequence of Slc26a9 suggests that ions interact with a low field-strength binding site. The inability to transport SO42– is thus probably related to the fact that interactions within the binding site, which does not contain positive countercharges to balance the negatively-charged substrate, may not be sufficiently strong for the coordination of divalent anions.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and functional properties.

claim: All other mammalian SLC26 family members harbor very similar predicted binding sites to that of Slc26a9, with the notable exception that they additionally contain a positively charged amino acid at the equivalent position of V393.
source: Remarkably, all other mammalian family members harbor very similar predicted binding sites to that of Slc26a9, with the notable exception that they additionally contain a positively charged amino acid at the equivalent position of V393, which is located on the N-terminal end of helix α10 (Figure 8C; Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is observed from homology models and sequence alignment.

claim: Homology models predict the positively charged side-chain at the equivalent position of V393 to reside very close to the substrate binding site in other mammalian SLC26 paralogs.
source: Homology models predict this side-chain to reside very close to the substrate binding site (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), and an arginine at the equivalent location, which likely contributes to anion interactions, is also found in the Cl–/HCO3– transporter SLC4A1/Band 3 (Arakawa et al., 2015) (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is observed from homology models and supported by a citation.

claim: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport HCO3- is particularly remarkable, since the nearly isosteric molecular anion NO3- is a transported substrate.
source: The inability of Slc26a9 to transport HCO3– is particularly remarkable, since the nearly isosteric molecular anion NO3– is a transported substrate (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is observed from the functional data.

claim: The equilibrium between HCO3- and CO32- could be perturbed at the binding site, with the large positive electrostatic potential stabilizing the divalent state of the ion, for which interactions with the anion binding site would not be sufficiently strong.
source: Although the pKa for the deprotonation of HCO3– is high (i.e. 10.3) and consequently the concentration of the divalent anion CO32– is negligible under physiological conditions, the equilibrium could be perturbed at the binding site, with the large positive electrostatic potential within the aqueous cavity stabilizing the divalent state of the ion, for which interactions with the anion binding site would not be sufficiently strong to make it a transported substrate.
evidence: This is speculated based on the electrostatic properties and binding site characteristics.

claim: The high homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common general architecture.
source: The high homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common general architecture and also implies that other family members may undergo similar conformational transitions to those shown here for Slc26a9T.
evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation.

claim: Other SLC26 family members may undergo similar conformational transitions to those shown for Slc26a9T.
source: The high homology between mammalian SLC26 paralogs suggests a common general architecture and also implies that other family members may undergo similar conformational transitions to those shown here for Slc26a9T.
evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation and structural similarity.

claim: The diversity of functional phenotypes in the SLC26 family could rely on comparatively small localized structural differences which impose variable energy barriers for conformational changes.
source: Therefore, the diversity of functional phenotypes ranging from uncoupled bidirectional uniport as observed in Slc26a9 (and possibly SLC26A7 and/or SLC26A11), to coupled exchangers such as SLC26A2/DTDST and SLC26A4/Pendrin, or even to the motor activity of SLC26A5/Prestin (Alper and Sharma, 2013), could rely on comparatively small localized structural differences which in turn impose variable energy barriers for conformational changes (Figure 8—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is speculated based on the structural and functional diversity.

claim: Uncoupled uniporters like Slc26a9 presumably possess small conformational energy barriers between inward and outward states in the presence or absence of substrate which would permit transition of an unloaded transporter.
source: Uncoupled uniporters like Slc26a9 presumably possess small conformational energy barriers between inward and outward states in the presence or absence of substrate which would permit transition of an unloaded transporter.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observed mechanism.

claim: For coupled transport, the presumed increase in ion binding affinity paired with an enlarged barrier prohibiting conformational transitions of the unloaded transport domain would itself lead to stoichiometric exchange.
source: In contrast, for coupled transport the presumed increase in ion binding affinity paired with an enlarged barrier prohibiting conformational transitions of the unloaded transport domain would itself lead to stoichiometric exchange.
evidence: This is speculated based on mechanistic principles.

claim: The electromotile motor function of SLC26A5/Prestin could be a consequence of an insurmountable energy barrier preventing the last phase of the transition to an outward-facing state.
source: In this view, the electromotile motor function of SLC26A5/Prestin could be a consequence of an insurmountable energy barrier preventing the last phase of the transition to an outward-facing state, in line with prior suggestions of SLC26A5/Prestin exhibiting an 'incomplete' transport cycle (Schaechinger and Oliver, 2007).
evidence: This is speculated based on the mechanism and supported by a citation.

claim: Electrophysiology experiments show instantaneous activity of Slc26a9T that is not obviously dependent on activating ligands.
source: Since our electrophysiology experiments show instantaneous activity of the transporter that is not obviously dependent on activating ligands (Figure 1B), the question concerning the regulation of Slc26a9 activity under physiological conditions is pertinent.
evidence: This is observed from electrophysiology data.

claim: A potential activation mechanism could be the mobilization of SLC26A9 from intracellular stores, which might be regulated by phosphorylation.
source: A potential activation mechanism could be the mobilization of SLC26A9 from intracellular stores, which might be regulated by phosphorylation, as suggested in a previous study (Dorwart et al., 2007) and which is also consistent with the predominantly intracellular localization of full-length Slc26a9 observed in our study (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is speculated based on previous studies and the observed localization.

claim: The IVS may harbor modifiable motif elements which can be involved in surface-trafficking regulation.
source: The fact that removal of the IVS results in significantly greater surface expression suggests that this region may harbor modifiable motif elements which can be involved in surface-trafficking regulation, but this hypothesis must be further evaluated in more physiologically relevant contexts.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observed effect of IVS deletion.
